items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bill Berry was in the group, that’s right. And Jake. Jake was an incredible drummer... I remember I took that job... Art Davis, the bass player. Jake Hanna.

ctx.x: Would have been mid to late sixties?
Yeah. That was… I remember I took that job after Janie and I got married, ‘cause I’d been on the road so much and I thought, well, I can take a subway to work here and…

oh, what’s his name, the guitar player whose place I took? He was moving out to California. Can’t think of his name now. And… Yeah, so Bob (unintelligible) an incredible musician. Bob Brookmeyer. Richie Kamuca, marvelous tenor player. Art Davis, the bass player. Jake Hanna. Jake made it possible for… He was so funny. God. I would think… sometimes I would get so depressed doing it. ‘Cause I felt like I was… that’s one of the reasons I never got to record with Miles Davis. He, he had called me once before. Anyway,…

items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Chuck Wayne and Jim Hall. Chuck Wayne refused to play. Now we’ve got two guys that refused to play the stuff. So you never heard so many bossa novas in your life with two guitar players going out.

ctx.x: Who was in the pit, in the show band?

In New York we had Billy Watrous, Danny Stiles and Bill Berry. Then we added like Ziggy Harrell and Roy Eldridge, and on sax we had Roger Pemberton, tenor, Shelly Gould, and Richie Kamuka. Then Richie had to figure out whether to add Zoot Sims or Al Cohn, then Jim Hall was the guitar, and he took off and we got Jim Raney or somebody like that. And Jimmy refused to play any of this rock & roll stuff for Sonny. He refused to do it. So they brought in another guy. So now we had two guitars. Chuck Wayne and Jim Hall.…
